title: When You're In Love: three recordings undone by a title clash
summary: His song, written with Lou Douglas, is recorded three times but never released because Johnny Mercer had a song with the same title.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: The rest of it was raised in the sand.

Yeah, the rest of it was raised in the sand. And it was just too pretty and it just wasn't the timing. It was the wrong time for it to come out. And the, I had worked with Lou Douglas for a while. Lou Douglas liked a lot of them. I had about, written about 20 songs by then. So, he came to my house one day and I, he went over the first five and said, I like all these five. Let me have them see what I can do. So, Tommy Leonetti came to town and he submitted one to Leonetti. And so Lou and Leonetti thought it was from Out of This World. And they said it was too close to the other old song, Out of This World. That is, the lyrics were. The music was totally different and they were crazy about the music. So, they got a lyric writer to write another lyric to it and he wrote, When You're In Love. We recorded the song in Universal Studios with Lee Gillette A&R and the record sound beautiful. Everybody was enthused. And somehow in my heart, I was sad. I didn't know what was the matter. I was sad. I had copied the score for Douglas. Douglas, Lou Douglas made the Rangers. So, I copied the score. I got such a good handwriting, a lot of the Rangers want me to copy for them. So, I was copying for Douglas and so he said, Charlie, you got a hit. But somehow or another, I felt depressed. I felt like it wasn't going to happen. Here's what it was. Johnny Mercer had written a song of the same title, totally different music, for the picture Seven Brides for Seven Brothers or something like that. Yeah. And they had it in that picture. So, when mine was at this part, at least the lyric writers had written the same title, same idea. They had never heard Johnny Mercer. Johnny Mercer had never heard this. And so, the record never was released. In the meanwhile, RCA Victor recorded with Frankie Lester singing. And here, Danny Bellock's band had recorded two. So, I had three records on the song and didn't make a dime and it wasn't released because of the similarity of titles. Because the other, there's an agreement between the publishers, if one comes out with the title first and the other one didn't know about it, and he comes out with the same title, he will automatically withdraw and leave the first one. So, I had, so, yeah, I got three recordings on the song and didn't make a, and that's what it was, that premonition.
It's too bad you couldn't have simply changed the title and used the same one.

Well, I told Archie, Archie Levinson has, he's the publisher, and I told him one day, I said, why don't we put my original lyric back on there? So, he said, well, he says, I don't know, we got it printed up and everything and they might release it someday. I said, I don't think they'll release it because it's similar to the titles. I'm still, I'm gonna still see them because the tune is a beautiful tune. I got it on the tape here, I want you to hear it.
